### Currency input
Shows a typed amount in the page's locale and currency once the field loses focus, and submits the plain number.

Component ID: `currency-input`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: A price field in a German shop takes data-currency="EUR" with inputmode="decimal" under lang="de" and shows 1.234,50 € after blur; a quantity field stays a number field.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-25); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-25, `llm.md#currency-input`): A data-currency ISO 4217 code on a text input; the amount shown with Intl.NumberFormat in the nearest lang and that currency on blur, the plain number in the locale's decimal mark on focus, typed and pasted amounts read in either decimal mark, a validity message for text with no digit that i18n can replace, saved and reset values formatted, a value property, and the plain number in the form data.

Web adaptation: The native value holds the formatted text, and a capture-phase formdata listener on the document swaps the field's entry for the plain number, so submits and new FormData(form) read a number while the field keeps its name. setCustomValidity reports text with no amount, so constraint validation and .validate show the message.

Known boundary: Typing and blur, focus editing, listener order, pasted amounts submitted with Enter, the validity message, saved and reset values and destroy() are checked in a browser, and the parsing rules in jsdom; mobile decimal keypads and spoken output remain unverified. Formatting happens on blur only, and a form that repeats a currency field's name gets one entry for them.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#currency-input).

#### Contract

Add `data-currency` with an ISO 4217 code, such as `EUR`, to an `<input>` of type `text`. `AutoInit()` starts every one. The locale comes from the nearest `lang`, or the browser's language without one. A code `Intl.NumberFormat` rejects leaves the field a plain text input.

When the field loses focus, it shows the amount rounded to the currency's fraction digits: under `lang="de"` with `EUR`, typing `1234.5` shows `1.234,50 €`. A page's `change` and `blur` listeners read the formatted text. When the field gains focus, it shows the plain number in the locale's decimal mark, without grouping or sign, such as `1234,5`, with the caret at the end.

Typed and pasted text keeps its digits, `.`, `,` and a leading `-` or `−`, and drops anything else, such as spaces, signs and letters. The last `.` or `,` is the decimal mark when it is followed by no more digits than the currency shows; every other separator groups. So `1234.5`, `1234,5`, `1.234,5` and `1,234.50` all read 1234.5, `1.234` reads 1234 for euros, and with yen, which has no fraction digits, every separator groups. Full-width digits from an IME and the locale's own digits read as digits. Text with no digit stays as typed, and the field reports itself invalid with `Enter an amount.` until it holds an amount or is empty, so `.validate` shows the message.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="field">
  <input id="price" name="price" type="text" inputmode="decimal" autocomplete="off" placeholder=" " data-currency="EUR">
  <label for="price">Price in euros</label>
</div>
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `i18n` | Object | `{ invalid: 'Enter an amount.' }` | `invalid` is the validity message for text that holds no amount. Markup sets it with `data-currency-input-options='{"i18n":{"invalid":"Betrag eingeben."}}'`. |

#### Methods

- `.destroy()`: Removes the listeners, clears the validity message and leaves the text as it is.

#### Also documented

The Currency input section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Properties.

#### Rules

- `currency-input-needs-a-text-field`: Put data-currency, with a currency code such as EUR, on an <input> of type text. Other input types reject a formatted amount such as 1.234,50 €, and AutoInit skips them; a <textarea> is not formatted.
